defaults.name: joystick_trim_follow_curve_y
defaults.info: Auto-calibrated elevator trim response curve. Captured by the Elevator Trim Calibration tool; used when 'Use Calibrated Trim Curve' is enabled.

defaults.name: joystick_trim_follow_curve_gain_y
defaults.info:
How far the stick sits from center for a given amount of out-of-trim - which sets how much force you feel holding against it. 100% is the aircraft's measured response, exactly as the calibration recorded it.

In 'Stays Centered' this affects out-of-trim force only; trimmed flight always rests the stick at center.

In 'Follows Trim' it also scales how far the resting position rides with airspeed. Raise it to exaggerate that trim-position cue, or lower it if the stick sits so far aft in slow flight that you run out of usable travel.

It does not change the calibration or the trim curve - trimming with the stick held never moves the nose, at any setting. Away from 100% a released stick delivers a small residual input, so a hands-off aircraft will not follow its trim quite exactly; in 'Follows Trim' this also shows up as slow drift when trimmed at the extremes of your calibrated speed range.

defaults.name: joystick_trim_follow_stick_position
defaults.info:
Where the stick rests when the aircraft is trimmed, with calibrated curves at multiple speeds.

'Follows Trim': the rest position rides the measured trim state - aft when trimmed for slow flight, forward when fast - like cable/trim-tab aircraft where the yoke is linked to the control surface.

'Stays Centered': trimmed flight always rests the stick at center - like moving-stabilizer, FBW or spring-cartridge aircraft where trim re-rigs the feel datum.

Force behavior is identical in both modes (trimmed = zero force, out-of-trim = force); only the resting geometry differs.
